name: Eggs in a Tomato, Sweet Potato & Kale Stew (Shakshuka) with Toast

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
227 g sweet potato
½ small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley
½ bunch kale

instructions.primary_message: Peel and coarsely grate sweet potato. Place in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and medium dice onion. Add to the bowl with the sweet potato and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add sweet potato and onion to the skillet. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves.

Once the veggies are tender, add half of the parsley, tomatoes, tomato sauce, water, and spices to the skillet. Stir to combine the stew and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, cook until slightly thickened, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (411 g) can diced tomatoes
1 (221 g) can tomato sauce
½ tsp cumin, ground
salt
black pepper
¼ tsp smoked paprika
¼ tsp cayenne pepper

instructions.primary_message: While the stew is simmering, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven. (Skip this step if you are using a toaster for the bread.)
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces.
When the stew has thickened slightly, add kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.

Using a stirring spoon, make a well in the stew for each egg; crack an egg into each well and season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook until the egg whites are firm but yolks are still soft, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, arrange bread on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven and broil, flipping halfway through, until toasted, about 2 minutes; remove from oven. (Alternatively, you can use a toaster.)
To serve, divide eggs, stew, and toast between plates. Top with Parmesan and reserved parsley. Enjoy!
